mission.statement: Build AskMyCV — a self-hosted, single-tenant Cloudflare Worker that turns the owner's CV into an AI-powered chat, deployable in one click by anyone with a Cloudflare and Anthropic account.
end_state: All functional requirements F1–F8 in docs/spec.md pass their done_when criteria when exercised against a running local Worker (wrangler dev or equivalent).
All twelve end-to-end acceptance scenarios (Test 1–Test 12 in docs/spec.md §12) pass against a running Worker with the mocked Anthropic and JWKS test harness.

A visitor without any login can open the Worker URL, ask a question, and receive a streamed, CV-grounded answer; an owner can complete first-time setup and edit their config later through a Cloudflare Access-gated /admin route.
The repository contains a README with a working Deploy-to-Cloudflare button, an AGPL-3.0 LICENSE, a non-trivial cv.example.md, and a wrangler.toml declaring the STATE KV namespace binding.
Daily Anthropic spend is capped server-side, per-IP rate limits and bot-UA rejection are enforced, and the Anthropic API key never appears in any HTML response or log line.

Every user-facing surface (visitor chat page, owner setup form, owner admin form, error/expired/denied pages) is rendered through a shared view module that consumes a single design-tokens source; no view template embeds raw color, typography, or spacing literals.
invariants: The chat page (GET /) and chat API (POST /chat) MUST remain accessible without any authentication — recruiters must never encounter a login screen.

Owner-only routes (/setup, /admin, /admin/save) MUST cryptographically verify the Cloudflare Access JWT (signature against the configured JWKS, issuer matching *.cloudflareaccess.com, audience, expiration, and email) before granting access — header presence alone is never sufficient.
The Anthropic API key MUST be read only from KV, never embedded in source, environment variables, wrangler vars blocks, HTML responses, or log output.
Daily Anthropic spend is hard-capped at the owner-configured daily_budget_usd; once met, /chat returns 503 until UTC midnight without contacting Anthropic.
All in-app UI text, code comments, and documentation are in English.
The product is licensed AGPL-3.0; the LICENSE file at the repo root reflects this.

Tests run inside a Cloudflare-Workers-compatible runtime (miniflare via @cloudflare/vitest-pool-workers), not bare Node — KV semantics, Request/Response streaming, and Web Crypto behave as on production Workers.

moat.primary: Open-source, one-click self-hosted distribution with BYOK keeps inference cost predictable for the owner while making the product itself a portfolio signal — competitors building shared SaaS variants inherit per-user costs and centralized data risk that AskMyCV's architecture refuses by construction.

health_metrics.healthy_when: Owner reaches a running Worker URL via the Deploy-to-Cloudflare button without any terminal or wrangler command.
Each owner's Anthropic key lives only in their own KV namespace; the repository contains no shared-key code paths.
daily_budget_usd is enforced as a hard ceiling and verifiable by pre-seeding spend:<today> >= budget and observing HTTP 503 with zero Anthropic calls.
Every view template imports from the single design-tokens module; grep finds zero raw hex color literals and zero raw px/rem dimension literals in view template files.

moat.priority: above execution speed, below mission invariants

legal: AGPL-3.0 license terms apply to all source — derivative network deployments must remain open source.
No telemetry, analytics, or third-party tracking is added; the Worker never phones home to any service the project maintainers operate.
Visitor IPs used for rate limiting are stored only in transient KV keys with auto-expiry; no long-term visitor logging.
ethical_boundaries: Never weaken JWT verification (e.g., skip signature check, accept unsigned tokens, trust header presence alone) under any circumstance.
Never log, render, or otherwise expose the Anthropic API key in any response, error message, or log line.
Never make the chat page or chat API require authentication — that would break the product's primary use case.
escalation_triggers: A goal requires creating or paying for any external service account, domain, or third-party subscription.
A done_when criterion or business constraint in docs/spec.md cannot be met without weakening an invariant.

A required dependency (e.g., the jose JWT library, the Anthropic SDK pricing constants, @cloudflare/vitest-pool-workers, @anthropic-ai/sdk) has materially changed shape since the spec was written and the change cannot be absorbed without a spec amendment.
pivot_conditions: Cloudflare deprecates Workers KV or the Deploy-to-Cloudflare flow such that the single-click self-deploy story no longer works.
Anthropic removes the Claude API surface or pricing the spec assumes (Haiku 1/0.10/5 per M tokens, Sonnet 3/0.30/15) without a drop-in replacement.
Cloudflare Access changes its JWT issuance contract (issuer host, JWKS endpoint, claim shape) in a way the spec's verification logic cannot accommodate.
external_dependencies: Owners must hold their own Cloudflare account, GitHub account, and Anthropic account with ~$5 in credits — Strategos does not provision these.
Owners configure Cloudflare Access policies in their own dashboard after first deploy — Strategos does not control Cloudflare Access state from inside the Worker.

phases.name: Plan & Foundation
phases.rationale: Architecture grounded in real CF Workers + Anthropic API capabilities, then a buildable foundation with the right test runtime, then a coherent UI/UX template set. Behavior code in later phases plugs into a stable visual + verification baseline.

phases.name: Auth & Setup
phases.rationale: JWT verification + the unconfigured→configured state machine + the /setup form behavior — wired into the templates from G3 so the visual layer does not need to be re-invented per goal.

phases.name: Public Chat
phases.rationale: Once configured, the public chat experience is the product's primary use case. Visual layer comes from G3; this goal wires SSE streaming, Anthropic mock dispatch, and prompt construction into the chat-page template.

phases.name: Safety & Admin
phases.rationale: Anti-abuse/budget and admin editing both operate on the live chat surface and the configured KV state; they can be done in parallel after G5 lands.

phases.name: Errors & Acceptance
phases.rationale: Error pages, Anthropic failure handling, the 12 end-to-end scenarios, and the deliverables polish are last because they exercise the whole surface and verify nothing earlier was degraded.

goals.name: Architecture & test-harness design (grounded in real CF + Anthropic APIs)
goals.description: Produce a concrete architectural design document for the Worker before any code is written. The artifact must be grounded in real Cloudflare Workers runtime capabilities (KVNamespace API surface, ExecutionContext, Request/Response streaming, Web Crypto subtle availability, miniflare/wrangler local runtime contract) and the real Anthropic Messages API shape (the request body fields the Worker will send — model, system, messages, max_tokens, stream — the SSE event types Anthropic emits — message_start, content_block_delta, message_delta, message_stop — and the prompt-caching cache_control surface). The document fixes the implementation stack (TypeScript Cloudflare Worker, wrangler, vitest with @cloudflare/vitest-pool-workers, jose for JWT verification, @anthropic-ai/sdk for Anthropic calls), the file/module layout, the KV key schema (config, secrets, setup_window_start, spend:<UTC-date>, ratelimit:<ip>:<hour>), the routing approach (single fetch handler dispatching by URL path), the state machine transitions from docs/spec.md §8, the test harness contracts (controllable Anthropic mock that mirrors @anthropic-ai/sdk's Messages.create signature and the real SSE event stream; controllable JWKS mock that issues jose-compatible signed JWTs), and the pricing constants for cost tracking. Subsequent goals consume this as their planning baseline so the project stays coherent across separate agent sessions.

produces.description: Architecture & test-harness design: stack choice, module layout, KV schema, routing, state machine wiring, mock contracts (matching real @anthropic-ai/sdk + jose + Workers runtime shapes), pricing constants.

docs/architecture.md explicitly references docs/spec.md and names every functional requirement F1 through F8 by identifier.
docs/architecture.md enumerates the KV keys the Worker uses (config, secrets, setup_window_start, spend:<date>, and the rate-limit key family) and gives a one-line schema/purpose for each.

docs/architecture.md cites concrete Cloudflare Workers runtime APIs — at minimum KVNamespace (get/put/delete with options including expirationTtl), ExecutionContext.waitUntil for background spend writes, ReadableStream / TransformStream for SSE, and crypto.subtle availability for jose — and names the local-runtime contract used in tests (miniflare via @cloudflare/vitest-pool-workers).

docs/architecture.md cites the real Anthropic Messages API shape: the request fields model, system, messages, max_tokens, stream; the SSE event types message_start, content_block_delta, message_delta, message_stop; and the prompt-caching cache_control field on the system block (with the rationale for using it on the cv_markdown to reduce input-token cost per docs/spec.md §14).

docs/architecture.md describes how the Worker injects a test-only JWKS endpoint and a test-only Anthropic base URL so the test harness in docs/spec.md §12 is satisfiable without monkey-patching globals — the injection mechanism is named (e.g. via env binding or factory parameter) and the production default is named.

docs/architecture.md lists the four state-machine states from docs/spec.md §8 (unconfigured_no_access, unconfigured_with_access, configured, setup_window_expired) and the transition triggers between them.

An executor implementing G3 (UI/UX) can read docs/architecture.md and find the four user-facing surfaces (visitor chat page, owner setup form, owner admin form, error/expired pages) and the state machine that governs which surface is rendered when.
An executor implementing G5 (chat) can read docs/architecture.md and know the Anthropic request body shape and SSE event types — the Anthropic mock is contract-equivalent to the real API, not a stub.

goals.name: UI/UX foundation — design system & view templates
goals.description: Design and build the visual + interaction layer for every user-facing surface as a coherent product — not stitched HTML inside individual route handlers. Four surfaces are in scope per docs/spec.md: (1) visitor chat page rendered at GET / when configured (the recruiter-facing surface — owner name, headline, optional location, optional LinkedIn/GitHub/PDF anchors, at least three suggested-question controls, unobtrusive always-reachable input + submit, streamed assistant responses with [cv] citation tags styled as small chips); (2) owner setup instructions page rendered at GET / when no config and no Access JWT (step-by-step Access configuration walkthrough with the strings Cloudflare Access, /setup, /admin and a visible warning against gating the chat path, plus a continue affordance); (3) owner setup form rendered at GET / when no config but with valid JWT (display_name, headline, anthropic_api_key, cv_markdown required; location, linkedin_url, github_url, pdf_cv_url, accent_color optional; advanced/collapsible: model choice, daily_budget_usd, max_msgs_per_hour); (4) owner admin form at GET /admin (same fields as setup, pre-filled, with anthropic_api_key optional on edit); plus the error/expired/denied pages (expired setup window naming setup_window_start; Access denial pages distinguishing email_mismatch, aud_mismatch, team_domain_mismatch, signature_invalid, no_jwt). Produce a shared design-token set (typography scale, color palette honoring optional accent_color, spacing rhythm, radius, motion), a small reusable component primitive set (button, input, textarea, card, chip, anchor, error banner, code/citation tag, suggested-question chip, streamed-message bubble), and a template-rendering helper that all route handlers in later goals consume — so G4–G9 wire behavior into existing templates instead of authoring new HTML per route. Keep it server-rendered (no SPA framework); the only client-side JS is minimal sprinkles for SSE consumption on the chat page and Access-cookie polling on the setup instructions page.

produces.description: UI system marker — the views module re-exports the four page templates (chat-page, setup-instructions, setup-form, admin-form, error-page) and the shared primitive helpers; the commit also includes the design-tokens module, the streaming-message client sprinkle, and view-rendering tests.

done_when.criteria: The views module exports a callable template for each of the four user-facing surfaces (visitor chat page, setup instructions, setup form, admin form) and the error/expired/denied page family — each accepts a typed props object describing the data the surface needs and returns rendered HTML.

A design-tokens module exists and defines, at minimum, a typography scale, a color palette that honors an optional accent_color prop, spacing/radius scales, and motion/transition values — all referenced by name from the page templates, not duplicated as literals.

The chat-page template, when given the configured props (display_name, headline, optional location, optional linkedin_url/github_url/pdf_cv_url, suggested_questions), produces HTML that contains: the display name and headline as plain text; anchor tags whose href equals each provided URL; at least 3 suggested-question controls; an input or textarea control and a submit control; and a styled element family for streamed assistant messages including a citation-token tag (e.g. [cv]) styled as a small chip.

The setup-instructions template includes the literal strings "Cloudflare Access", "/setup", and "/admin", a visible warning that the chat/root path must NOT be gated, and a continue affordance plus a polling/reload mechanism (verifiable in the rendered HTML/JS) so the page detects when the owner has authenticated.

The setup-form template renders input controls whose names are display_name, headline, anthropic_api_key, cv_markdown (required) and location, linkedin_url, github_url, pdf_cv_url, accent_color (optional), with the advanced fields (model, daily_budget_usd, max_msgs_per_hour) inside a collapsible section.

The admin-form template renders the same field set as the setup form, pre-filled with provided config props, and treats anthropic_api_key as optional (empty = no change), with helper text reflecting that.

The error/expired/denied page family includes: an expired-setup-window page that contains wording about the expired window, the literal key name "setup_window_start", and a reference to the Cloudflare dashboard; an Access-denial page that accepts a reason prop and renders distinct wording for at least email_mismatch, aud_mismatch, team_domain_mismatch, signature_invalid, and no_jwt.

Every view template file under src/views/ imports from the design-tokens module (verifiable by grep). Every view template file under src/views/ contains zero raw hex color literals matching /#[0-9a-fA-F]{3,8}/ and zero raw px or rem numeric literals — all visual values resolve from named tokens.
View-rendering tests exist that snapshot or assert on the structural criteria above for all four surfaces plus the error family, and run inside the workers pool.
pnpm build, pnpm typecheck, and pnpm test all succeed with exit code 0; pnpm test reports >= the baseline test count from G2 plus the new view-rendering tests.

behavior_scenarios: A recruiter opens the deployed Worker URL, sees the owner's name and headline in a typographic hierarchy that feels intentional, scans three or more suggested-question chips, clicks one, and watches the streamed response appear in a message bubble with [cv] citations rendered as small inline chips.

goals.name: Auth + setup state machine behavior (F2 + F3)
goals.description: Wire the unconfigured → configured state machine into the templates from G3 per docs/spec.md §8 and §9 (F2, F3). This covers: detecting Cloudflare Access JWT in the cf-access-jwt-assertion header, verifying signature against the configured JWKS (via the test harness in tests, via Cloudflare's published JWKS in production), validating iss matches *.cloudflareaccess.com, validating exp, and (post-setup) validating email/aud/team-domain match the values recorded at setup time; rendering the setup-instructions template from G3 in state A; rendering the setup-form template from G3 in state B; accepting POST /setup with a real Anthropic test call (via @anthropic-ai/sdk against the mock in tests) to validate the submitted key, enforcing field bounds (cv_markdown between 200 and 50000 chars), persisting config (including access_email, access_aud, access_team_domain) and secrets to KV, and refusing POST /setup once config exists; recording setup_window_start on the first state-A request and emitting the expired-window template from G3 once 30 minutes have elapsed. All paths exercised by acceptance tests 1–5 in docs/spec.md §12 must pass.

done_when.criteria: GET / with empty KV and no cf-access-jwt-assertion header returns HTTP 200 by rendering the setup-instructions template from G3 — the response body contains the literal strings "Cloudflare Access", "/setup", "/admin", and the chat-path warning required by F2.
GET / with empty KV and no JWT does not return any HTML form field whose name is anthropic_api_key or cv_markdown.
After the first GET / under state A, the KV key setup_window_start is set to a recent timestamp.

GET / with empty KV and a valid JWT (signature cryptographically verified against the harness JWKS, iss=*.cloudflareaccess.com, not expired) returns HTTP 200 by rendering the setup-form template from G3 — the body contains HTML input controls whose names include display_name, headline, anthropic_api_key, and cv_markdown.
POST /setup without a valid JWT returns HTTP 403 and the KV namespace does not contain a config or secrets entry after the request.

POST /setup with a valid JWT but missing required fields (display_name, headline, anthropic_api_key, cv_markdown) returns HTTP 400 with a body identifying the missing field(s) and does not persist config.

POST /setup with a valid JWT and an Anthropic key that the test-harness Anthropic mock rejects on the test call returns HTTP 400 with a body identifying anthropic_api_key as the problem and does not persist config or secrets. The captured outgoing test-call request body has the documented Anthropic Messages API shape (model, system, messages, max_tokens fields present).
POST /setup with a valid JWT, cv_markdown shorter than 200 characters returns HTTP 400; cv_markdown longer than 50000 characters returns HTTP 400.

POST /setup with a valid JWT and valid fields returns HTTP 200, writes config (containing access_email, access_aud, access_team_domain matching the JWT's claims) and secrets to KV, and the 200 response body contains the public worker URL and the literal path "/admin".
POST /setup after config is already present in KV returns HTTP 403 regardless of JWT validity, and does not modify config.

With setup_window_start pre-seeded to >30 minutes ago and config absent, GET / returns HTTP 200 by rendering the expired-window template from G3 — body contains wording about an expired setup window, the literal key name "setup_window_start", and a reference to the Cloudflare dashboard; POST /setup in this state returns the expired-window error.
After deleting setup_window_start from KV (simulated recovery), GET / no longer returns the expired-window page.

pnpm build, pnpm typecheck, and pnpm test all succeed with exit code 0; pnpm test reports >= the baseline test count from G3 plus the new tests covering acceptance scenarios 1–5 in docs/spec.md §12, and the new tests run inside the workers pool.

behavior_scenarios: First-time owner hits the Worker URL with no JWT, sees the G3 setup-instructions surface naming /setup and /admin and the chat-path warning, configures Access in their Cloudflare dashboard, returns, authenticates, sees the G3 setup form, submits valid fields, lands on a confirmation page showing the public URL and the /admin link.

goals.name: Public chat behavior (F4)
goals.description: Wire the visitor-facing chat behavior into the chat-page template from G3 per docs/spec.md §9 F4 and §12 Test 6. GET / in the configured state renders the chat-page template with the owner's display_name, headline, optional location, optional LinkedIn/GitHub/PDF anchor tags, the suggested-question controls, and the input + submit — all reachable without any authentication. POST /chat is a Server-Sent Events endpoint: accept JSON {messages: [{role, content}]}, reject malformed bodies with 400, drop oldest messages beyond a 12-turn cap, truncate any single message to 1500 characters before sending to Anthropic, cap max_tokens at 512, construct a system prompt that contains the configured cv_markdown verbatim (with prompt-caching cache_control per G1's research) plus behavioral instructions (first person; refuse out-of-CV questions with a redirect to ask the owner directly; mark factual claims with a citation token such as [cv]; refuse instruction-injection / prompt extraction; politely decline off-topic). Stream the Anthropic response back to the client as SSE, consuming the message_start / content_block_delta / message_delta / message_stop events from the @anthropic-ai/sdk stream and emitting browser-friendly SSE chunks.

done_when.criteria: GET / with config present in KV returns HTTP 200 by rendering the chat-page template from G3 — the body contains the configured display_name, headline, and (when set) location as plain text.
When linkedin_url, github_url, or pdf_cv_url are present in config, GET / renders anchor tags whose href attributes equal those URLs.

GET / under the configured state renders at least 3 clickable suggested-question elements and an input control plus a submit control, and never returns any HTML form field whose name is anthropic_api_key.

POST /chat with a realistic browser User-Agent and a well-formed JSON body containing a non-empty messages array returns HTTP 200 with response header Content-Type: text/event-stream; the body is consumed as a stream and at least one SSE event chunk is parseable before the mocked upstream resolves fully (verified inside the workers pool).
POST /chat with an empty body, missing messages, or an empty messages array returns HTTP 400 without contacting the Anthropic mock.
POST /chat with a messages array containing more than 12 entries: the captured Anthropic mock request contains at most 12 messages, with the oldest dropped.
POST /chat with a single visitor message exceeding 1500 characters: the captured Anthropic mock request truncates the message content to 1500 characters.

The captured Anthropic mock request always has max_tokens <= 512 and its system field contains the configured cv_markdown verbatim, plus instructions covering: first-person voice, refusing out-of-CV questions with a redirect to ask the owner directly, marking factual claims with a citation token, refusing instruction-injection / prompt extraction, and politely declining off-topic requests.
Acceptance Test 6 from docs/spec.md §12 is implemented as an automated test inside the workers pool and passes.
pnpm build, pnpm typecheck, and pnpm test all succeed with exit code 0; pnpm test reports >= the baseline test count from G4 plus the new F4 / Test 6 tests.

behavior_scenarios: Recruiter clicks a link, sees the owner's name, headline, and three suggested questions, clicks one, watches the first SSE event arrive and stream into the chat-page message bubble, asks a follow-up referring to the CV, and reads an answer that quotes a [cv] citation chip.
Visitor sends a request with no messages array — receives 400 immediately and the Anthropic mock records zero calls.
Visitor sends a 13-message conversation — the captured Anthropic call shows only the last 12 messages and the system prompt still contains the full CV markdown.
goals.discovery_notes: Reads docs/spec.md §9 F4 and §12 Test 6 inside the workspace. The Anthropic client is @anthropic-ai/sdk used in streaming mode; the SSE bridge consumes message_start / content_block_delta / message_delta / message_stop events per G1's architecture and re-emits browser-friendly SSE chunks. Per-IP rate-limiting, daily-budget enforcement, and bot/CLI rejection live in G6 — this goal must implement the chat path coherently but does not include rate-limit or budget logic.
goals.baseline_state: After G4: state machine + setup flow green, chat-page template exists but no chat behavior wired.

goals.name: Anti-abuse + daily budget cap (F6 + F7)
goals.description: Add the cost ceiling and abuse-resistance layer per docs/spec.md §9 F6, F7 and §12 Tests 7–9. Track cumulative cost per UTC day in KV under spend:<UTC-date>, computing each request's cost from the input/cached/output token counts reported by the Anthropic message_delta / message_stop events and the model-appropriate pricing (Haiku 1 / 0.10 / 5; Sonnet 3 / 0.30 / 15 per million tokens) per docs/spec.md §9 F6. When the day's spend meets or exceeds config.daily_budget_usd, reject /chat with 503 until UTC midnight, without contacting Anthropic. Enforce a per-IP rate limit (default 30 requests/hour, configurable via config.max_msgs_per_hour) returning 429 once exceeded, with the rate-limit key auto-expiring at the hour rollover via KV expirationTtl. Reject /chat requests whose User-Agent header is empty, very short, or matches known CLI/bot user agents (curl, wget, python-requests, httpie, go-http) with 403, without contacting Anthropic. Reject /chat with garbage input (over 100 characters and more than 70% uppercase) with 400. Reject /chat with serialized message bodies exceeding 100KB with 400 or 413. Spend write failures (via ExecutionContext.waitUntil so the visitor's streamed response is not coupled to KV write success) must not break the visitor's streamed response.

done_when.criteria: After each successful POST /chat with mocked Anthropic token usage, the KV key spend:<today-UTC> increases monotonically and is set with an expirationTtl of at least 24 hours.

With spend:<today> pre-seeded to a value >= config.daily_budget_usd, POST /chat returns HTTP 503 and the Anthropic mock records zero calls; after resetting spend:<today> to 0, POST /chat succeeds again.

Given known mocked token counts, the persisted increment equals (input_tokens * input_rate + cached_tokens * cached_rate + output_tokens * output_rate) / 1_000_000 within 5% tolerance, where the rates are model-appropriate (Haiku 1 / 0.10 / 5; Sonnet 3 / 0.30 / 15).

POST /chat with User-Agent of curl/8.0.0, python-requests/2.31.0, or no User-Agent header returns HTTP 403 and the Anthropic mock records zero calls; POST /chat with a realistic browser User-Agent succeeds (subject to other limits).

With config.max_msgs_per_hour set to N, sending N successful POST /chat requests from the same simulated IP succeeds; the (N+1)th from the same IP within the hour returns HTTP 429 and the Anthropic mock records exactly N calls; after the hour-window key is cleared, subsequent requests from the same IP succeed again.

POST /chat with a single message whose content exceeds 100 characters and is more than 70% uppercase returns HTTP 400 without contacting Anthropic (per docs/spec.md §9 F4 done_when; this threshold also subsumes the §9 F7 5000-character check).
POST /chat with a messages array whose total serialized size exceeds 100 KB returns HTTP 400 or 413 without contacting Anthropic.
Simulating a KV put failure during the spend update path does not cause the visitor's POST /chat response to fail — the streamed body is delivered fully and the response is still 2xx.
Acceptance Tests 7, 8, and 9 from docs/spec.md §12 are implemented as automated tests inside the workers pool and pass.
pnpm build, pnpm typecheck, and pnpm test all succeed with exit code 0; pnpm test reports >= the baseline test count from G5 plus the new F6/F7/Test 7-9 tests.

behavior_scenarios: An attacker scripts curl in a loop against /chat — every request is rejected with 403 because of the User-Agent check, and the Anthropic mock receives zero traffic.
A legitimate recruiter exceeds the per-hour message limit by accident — the next message returns 429, but after an hour they can chat again without intervention from the owner.

The Anthropic mock returns large token counts in a single response that brings spend:<today> over the budget — the very next request returns 503 with no Anthropic call until UTC midnight rolls the key over.
goals.discovery_notes: Reads docs/spec.md §9 F6, F7, §10 (non-functional bounds), and §12 Test 7–Test 9 inside the workspace. Pricing constants live in a single module so changing rates is a one-file edit (docs/spec.md §14 informational target). Spend writes use ExecutionContext.waitUntil per G1's architecture so the streamed response is not blocked on KV.
goals.baseline_state: After G5: public chat green; no rate limit, no budget enforcement, no bot-UA filter implemented yet.

goals.name: Admin / configuration editing behavior (F5)
goals.description: Wire the GET /admin and POST /admin/save behavior into the admin-form template from G3 per docs/spec.md §9 F5 and §12 Tests 10–11. Gate both routes by strict identity match against the JWT recorded during setup: signature valid against the configured JWKS, iss matches config.access_team_domain, aud matches config.access_aud, email matches config.access_email. On any failure, render the G3 access-denial template with the reason prop set to the specific failure mode (email_mismatch, aud_mismatch, team_domain_mismatch, signature_invalid, no_jwt). On success, GET /admin renders the admin-form template pre-filled with current config values; POST /admin/save updates config in KV. The anthropic_api_key field is optional on edit: empty means "no change"; a non-empty value is validated against Anthropic via @anthropic-ai/sdk against the mock test call before replacing the existing secret, and a failing validation returns 400 without overwriting the stored secret. Changes take effect on the next /chat request with no redeploy.

done_when.criteria: GET /admin with config in KV and no cf-access-jwt-assertion header returns HTTP 403.
GET /admin with an invalid-signature JWT returns HTTP 403 and the body contains wording identifying signature_invalid.
GET /admin with a JWT whose email does not match config.access_email returns HTTP 403 and the body contains wording identifying email_mismatch (the word "email").
GET /admin with a JWT whose aud does not match config.access_aud returns HTTP 403 and the body contains wording identifying aud_mismatch (the word "aud").
GET /admin with a JWT whose iss/team domain does not match config.access_team_domain returns HTTP 403 and the body contains wording identifying team_domain_mismatch.

GET /admin with a fully matching JWT returns HTTP 200 by rendering the admin-form template from G3 — the body contains HTML input controls whose values reflect the current config (display_name, headline, cv_markdown at minimum).
POST /admin/save without a fully matching JWT returns HTTP 403 and KV is unchanged.
POST /admin/save with a fully matching JWT and a new headline writes the updated config to KV and returns HTTP 200.
POST /admin/save with the anthropic_api_key field absent or empty does not overwrite the existing secrets entry in KV.

POST /admin/save with a non-empty anthropic_api_key that the Anthropic mock rejects on the test call returns HTTP 400 and does not overwrite the existing secrets entry. The captured outgoing test-call request body has the documented Anthropic Messages API shape (model, system, messages, max_tokens fields present).
After a successful POST /admin/save that changes cv_markdown, the next POST /chat captures an Anthropic request whose system field contains the new cv_markdown content and not the old content.
Acceptance Tests 10 and 11 from docs/spec.md §12 are implemented as automated tests inside the workers pool and pass.
pnpm build, pnpm typecheck, and pnpm test all succeed with exit code 0; pnpm test reports >= the baseline test count from G6 plus the new F5/Test 10-11 tests.

behavior_scenarios: Owner navigates to /admin a week after setup, authenticates via the same Cloudflare Access policy, edits the CV with a new role through the G3 admin form, submits — and the next visitor chat reflects the new role without any redeploy.

A different person who happens to be on the owner's Access team but with a different email visits /admin, lands on the G3 access-denial page with reason=email_mismatch, and cannot read or edit configuration.
Owner attempts to update the Anthropic key with an invalid value — receives 400 and finds that the existing key still works for visitor chats.
goals.discovery_notes: Reads docs/spec.md §9 F5 and §12 Test 10–Test 11 inside the workspace. Reuses the JWT verification helpers introduced in G4; this goal adds the strict-identity-match layer on top of plain signature validity. All HTML is rendered through G3's view module.
goals.baseline_state: After G6: chat + safety green; /admin and /admin/save not implemented yet, admin-form template from G3 ready to be wired.

goals.name: Error states, Anthropic failure handling & non-functional bounds
goals.description: Round out the error-state surface and resilience per docs/spec.md §9 F8, §10 (non-functional requirements), and §12 Test 12. Every error page renders through G3's error/denial templates. When the Anthropic mock returns HTTP 500 or times out, POST /chat must return a non-2xx response with a JSON body containing an error field, within a bounded time, and the Worker must continue serving subsequent requests successfully. The Anthropic API key must never appear in any HTML response (GET /, GET /admin, GET /setup) or in the Worker's stdout/stderr logs. Spend-write failures must not break visitor responses (already covered by G6; this goal verifies the cross-cutting behavior under stress and assembles the unified error-page taxonomy).

done_when.criteria: The expired-setup-window page (state D) contains: wording that the setup window has expired, the literal key name "setup_window_start", and a reference to the Cloudflare dashboard — verifiable by pre-seeding setup_window_start to >30 min ago and inspecting GET /.

Every /admin denial response distinguishes its failure mode in the response body: at minimum the strings or labels email_mismatch, aud_mismatch, team_domain_mismatch, signature_invalid, and no_jwt are each producible by an appropriate JWT/header configuration.

With the Anthropic mock configured to return HTTP 500, POST /chat returns a non-2xx response whose body parses as JSON containing an error field, and a subsequent POST /chat (with the mock reset to 200) returns HTTP 200.
With the Anthropic mock configured to time out, POST /chat returns a non-2xx response within a bounded time (no hung connection); the test asserts response within 30 seconds.
GET /, GET /admin (with matching JWT and config present), and GET /setup (in state B with valid JWT) all return responses whose bodies do not contain the configured Anthropic key string.
The Worker's captured stdout/stderr during a full test run does not contain the configured Anthropic key string.
Simulating a KV put failure during the spend update path leaves POST /chat returning a 2xx streamed response (cross-checks G6's behavior at the boundary).
Acceptance Test 12 from docs/spec.md §12 is implemented as an automated test inside the workers pool and passes.
pnpm build, pnpm typecheck, and pnpm test all succeed with exit code 0; pnpm test reports >= the baseline test count from G7 plus the new F8 / §10 / Test 12 tests.

behavior_scenarios: An owner whose setup window expired sees a clear page telling them which KV key to delete and where (Cloudflare dashboard) — they recover without re-deploying.
Anthropic's API briefly returns 500 — a visitor sees a clean JSON error instead of a hung request, refreshes after a minute, and the next request succeeds because Anthropic recovered.

goals.discovery_notes: Reads docs/spec.md §9 F8, §10, and §12 Test 12 inside the workspace. Existing error templates from G3 are reused here; do not regress any criterion from earlier goals.

goals.name: Deliverables, README polish & full acceptance pass
